title: Queue burst memory bridge calls and resync canonical entries missed by Hindsight mirror

reproduction.before_fix: When a closed meeting writes two persona entries (p-alpha-meeting, p-beta-meeting) and one institutional meeting minute (mem-meeting-minute) together, services/memory/hindsight_index.py spawned up to MAX_MIRROR_WORKERS=4 concurrent retain threads while services/openclaw-gateway-adapter/memory_llm_bridge.py acquired its max_concurrency=2 semaphore with blocking=False and immediately returned 429 concurrency_limit. mirror_entry exhausted its 3 retries (0.5s + 1.0s = 1.5s) while the first two 1.7s LLM calls were still in flight and dropped mem-meeting-minute (retained=2, failed=1, reason=hindsight_http_429) without a catch-up mechanism.
reproduction.after_fix: MemoryLlmBridge waits up to bounded slot_wait_seconds (default 15.0s via MEMORY_LLM_BRIDGE_SLOT_WAIT_SECONDS, bounded by remaining request deadline; 0.0 restores immediate non-blocking refusal) before returning 429 concurrency_limit; hindsight_index defaults PANTHEON_MEMORY_MIRROR_WORKERS=1, honours bounded HTTP 429 Retry-After in HindsightClient and mirror_entry, retains failed retains and invalidation tombstones in a bounded in-memory resync map (capped at MAX_PENDING_MIRRORS=256 entries and MAX_PENDING_RESYNC_BYTES=262144 bytes) retried through the shared bounded mirror worker pool on a non-overlapping backoff timer (at most once per 60s while pending_resync_count > 0, stopping when empty), preserves latest archive/supersede tombstones and revalidates current canonical store state after remote memory_units probes so archived or superseded entries are never resurrected by catch-up or recovery, exposes pending_resync_count and pending_resync_bytes via GET /api/memory/health, checks queue capacity before issuing remote memory_units queries for deferred entries, and schedules non-destructive startup catch-up scans in bounded background work so lifespan startup, health endpoints, and canonical writes never block on slow or unavailable Hindsight.

runtime_budget.storage_manifest_registration: not required (zero persistent files, tables, or queues added; verified by scripts/check_storage_manifest.py)
runtime_budget.in_memory_resync_map_payload_accounting: _PENDING_RESYNC_BYTES tracks UTF-8 JSON serialized payload bytes + 128B overhead per entry; oldest-first FIFO eviction enforces both len(_PENDING_RESYNC) <= 256 and sum(_PENDING_RESYNC_BYTES) <= 262144 (256 KB); cleared on mirror completion, invalidation, rebuild, or reset; no _MIRRORED_DOCS cache retained
runtime_budget.resync_timer_cadence_and_worker_routing: At most once per 60 seconds (exponential backoff 60s -> 120s -> 240s -> 300s cap) while pending_resync_count > 0; non-overlapping passes (_RESYNC_IN_PROGRESS) route retries through the shared bounded worker pool (PANTHEON_MEMORY_MIRROR_WORKERS, default 1); timer cancels when pending_resync_count reaches 0 or on service shutdown
runtime_budget.startup_catchup_continuation_budget: Schedules startup catch-up scans on a single bounded background daemon worker (memory-catchup), checks queue capacity before issuing remote memory_units queries so deferred entries never trigger remote reads while the queue is full, admits at most MAX_PENDING_MIRRORS=256 entries per pass into _PENDING, revalidates canonical store state and preserves tombstones before scheduling, and stores a single tuple reference (_CATCHUP_CONTINUATION) to rescan canonical stores on worker drain until deferred reaches 0
